title: Choice verification and output probability
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $V$ be a language of Boolean words, and let $x$ be a Boolean word. Suppose that for every word $u$ of length exactly $Q$, the concatenation $xu$ belongs to $V$ if and only if the run of $N$ on input $x$ under choices $u$ halts and outputs the one-symbol word $[\mathrm{true}]$. Suppose also that every run of $N$ on $x$ under a choice word of length exactly $T$ halts, and that $T\le Q$. Then the probability that $xu$ belongs to $V$ for a uniformly random Boolean word $u$ of length $Q$ equals the probability that $N$ outputs $[\mathrm{true}]$ on input $x$ under a uniformly random choice word of length $T$.
